name: Confluent, Inc. (an IBM company since 2026)
origin_detail: Spun out of LinkedIn: Jay Kreps, Neha Narkhede and Jun Rao created Apache Kafka at LinkedIn (open-sourced 2011) and founded Confluent in Mountain View in September 2014, announced in November 2014 with $6.9M from Benchmark, Data Collective and LinkedIn itself. Founders kept getting support requests from Kafka users.
openness_notes: Kafka itself is an Apache Software Foundation project (Apache-2.0, foundation-governed), and Confluent's early platform add-ons were Apache-2.0. The company then sold proprietary enterprise tooling and Confluent Cloud (open core). From Confluent Platform 5.1 (December 2018), Schema Registry, REST Proxy, KSQL/ksqlDB and some connectors moved to the source-available Confluent Community License; Kafka stayed Apache-2.0. Current level 2: OSI core it does not solely control, with non-OSI and proprietary layers on top.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 (Kafka at ASF; Confluent platform components)
license_history.note: Company said it would stay '100 percent open source' while planning some proprietary tools.

license_history.license: Confluent Community License (Schema Registry, REST Proxy, KSQL, some connectors); Kafka unchanged Apache-2.0
license_history.note: Applies to Confluent Platform 5.1+; prevents offering these components as a competing SaaS.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Narrow change: the core engine (Kafka) stayed under ASF governance, so cloud providers could keep offering managed Apache Kafka. No significant fork of the relicensed components was found.

exit_events.note: Priced 2021-06-23 at $36 (range $29-33), 23M shares, $828M raised; trading began 2021-06-24. Diluted valuation 'close to $12 billion' (Benzinga); last private valuation ~$4.5B (Series E, $250M, April 2020, led by Coatue).
Announced 2025-12-08 at $31/share cash (34% premium to the prior close of $23.14), enterprise value ~$11B; closed 2026-03-17. IBM's 10-Q shows $11,268M cash paid for Confluent common stock.

risk_events: 2018-12: Confluent Community License for several platform components
2021-2025: Shares fell from the $36 IPO price to $23.14 before IBM's bid; GAAP operating loss still $380M in 2025
2026-03-17: Independent company ended; acquired by IBM
robustness: The core technology (Kafka) is foundation-governed at the ASF and offered by many vendors and clouds, so users are not locked to Confluent. The company itself is now an IBM unit. At acquisition it had $1.17B revenue (+21%), Confluent Cloud at 56% of subscription revenue, 114% net retention and 6,500+ enterprise customers.
physical_science_relevance: Kafka is used for high-rate instrument and sensor streaming (e.g. telescope and accelerator data pipelines); Confluent sells the managed version.
openness_effect_assessment: Building on a foundation-governed Apache project gave Confluent a huge user base it did not need to defend with licence changes on the core; it restricted only its own add-ons. That narrower closing avoided a fork war but also meant hyperscalers could sell managed Kafka freely, and Confluent never reached GAAP profitability. Its value ended about where its IPO valuation started (~$11-12B).
key_takeaway: Confluent shows a middle path: keep the engine at a neutral foundation, monetize a cloud service and proprietary or source-available extras. It avoided the Elastic/Redis-style fork, grew to $1.17B in revenue, and was bought by IBM for ~$11B in March 2026. Together with HashiCorp, it shows IBM consolidating open-source-origin infrastructure companies, after Red Hat, as a strategy for enterprise AI.
